The provisional ADR-0025 citation is explicitly flagged 're-verified at drafting time' rather than asserted as an existing artifact, so it is not an unjustified phantom-ADR reference. No unjustified 'we will use X' statement was found.

design.md has a '## Constraint Compliance' section (lines 832-841, 6 rows: Protected-file write boundary, CI resilience, Doc-following, Version-bump discipline, No Registry/Epic A2 coupling, No file-presence mode selection), so the primary (TYPE-D, Critical) check path applies: every constraint requirements.md states must be reconciled in that section. At least three explicit, normatively-worded requirements.md constraints are absent from it: (a) the compatibility constraint at requirements.md lines 64-69 ('path-separator, encoding, and case-sensitivity semantics must be identical to Linux/macOS runners... path and case semantics must not depend on host OS'); (b) the Security Boundaries submodule/symlink constraint ('the resolver never dereferences a symlink or descends into a submodule's own working tree', requirements.md Security Boundaries bullet 4); (c) the Fail-6 credential-exclusion constraint ('Fail-6's Provider Binding check never reads sdd/provider-bindings.yaml's credentials block', requirements.md Security Boundaries bullet 5). None of the six Constraint Compliance rows maps to these three items (the closest, 'CI resilience', covers only shell-script set -u/pwd -P/tr -d '\r' hygiene, a distinct concern). The underlying design substance for all three constraints does exist elsewhere in the document (glob-normalization Design Decisions and REQ-009's parity harness for (a); Security Boundaries and the B4 STRIDE row in security-spec.md for (b); Security Boundaries bullet 5 and security-spec.md Secrets Management for (c)), so this is a completeness gap in the feature's own designated compliance-reconciliation artifact, not evidence of an unaddressed design concern in substance -- but per this check's explicit contract ('A constraint with no compliance statement is a Critical finding'), an incomplete Constraint Compliance table for named requirements.md constraints is the literal, cited failure mode: a reviewer or quality-gate evaluator relying on this table as the canonical constraint-reconciliation record would not see these three constraints affirmatively tracked.

design.md's '## Deployment / CI Plan' section (lines 821-830) covers only test-suite CI registration (5 new .sh/.ps1 pairs into tests/run-all.sh/.ps1 and .github/workflows/test.yml via human-copy, 'no new CI job/matrix dimension'). This feature's actual Gate rollout is functionally incremental/staged: REQ-004 defines a three-state capability-derived applicability model (disabled-legacy/advisory/required, ADR-0016) that governs whether check-component-coverage blocks the Implementation Gate at all for a given consuming project -- an explicit feature-flag-equivalent staged-rollout mechanism (design.md Architecture, Design Decisions 'Capability-derived, three-state Gate applicability'). The Deployment / CI Plan section itself does not describe or even cross-reference this staged-rollout mechanism, nor does it note the interaction with this repository's own current absence of project-context.yaml (investigation.md INV-002) and check-contract's tier-minimum set having no capability-state axis of its own (INV-018) -- i.e., how the newly-registered required-check-set entry will resolve to a safe 'disabled-legacy' evidence record via the ADR-0016 file-absence fallback for this repository's own immediate adoption, rather than an unexpected block. This information exists elsewhere in the document (Architecture, Design Decisions, Security Boundaries B5) but is not consolidated into, or cross-referenced from, the section this check's contract designates for deployment/rollout planning.

No schema changes are declared. design.md's Data Plan (lines 341-402) lists only file/JSON-shaped entities (component path config consumed not redefined, resolver output, ownership_digest, Gate evidence record, human-copy staging files) and states 'Existing Data Affected' items are protected files that are read but never written directly -- no database column/table change anywhere. infra-spec.md's Data Residency and Retention section confirms explicitly: 'No database, no migration, no runtime storage anywhere in this feature (design.md Data Plan).' design.md's '## External Integrations' section states 'None.
